headlines.title: Duke Energy (DUK) Following Rate Approval Has Its Valuation Back In Focus
headlines.summary: Duke Energy rate decision and why it matters for the stock Duke Energy (DUK) just secured approval for a 9% electricity rate increase from the North Carolina Utilities Commission, with new protections tied to large power users such as data centers. Duke Energy’s recent regulatory win arrives after a steady run in the market, with the share price up 5.99% over the past 30 days and 9.15% across 90 days, while total shareholder return over 5 years sits at 65.

headlines.title: Duke Energy gears up for Thanksgiving week storms, urges Carolinas customers to prepare for potential outages
headlines.summary: Duke Energy is preparing to respond to potential damage and power outages in the Carolinas caused by high winds and rain.

headlines.title: Duke Energy (DUK) Stock Could Be 23% Overvalued Despite New Carolinas Resource Plan
headlines.summary: Duke Energy has built a solid multi‑year return profile, and the latest share price near US$130.96 keeps it firmly on income investors' radar. That performance now raises a straightforward question for you as a shareholder or potential buyer: whether the current valuation is still supported by the utility's dividend stream. Over the past 5 years, Duke Energy has returned 63.5%, which puts meaningful weight on whether the cash paid out to investors can justify that journey.

headlines.title: Should 9% Rate Increase Require Action From Duke Energy (DUK) Investors?
headlines.summary: The North Carolina Utilities Commission has approved a 9% rate increase for Duke Energy, effective January 1, 2027, alongside new rules that require large users such as data centers to fund dedicated infrastructure upfront and protect customers from stranded asset risk.

description: Duke Energy Corporation, through its subsidiaries, operates as an energy company in the United States. The company operates through two segments: Electric Utilities and Infrastructure (EU&I); and Gas Utilities and Infrastructure (GU&I). The EU&I segment generates, transmits, distributes, and sells electricity to customers in the Southeast and Midwest regions. It generates electricity through coal, hydroelectric, natural gas, oil, renewables, and nuclear fuel. This segment also engages in the wholesale of electricity to municipalities, electric cooperative utilities, and other load-serving entities. The GU&I segment distributes natural gas to customers in the residential, commercial, industrial, and power generation natural gas sectors; and invests in pipeline transmission projects, renewable natural gas projects, and natural gas storage facilities. The company was formerly known as Duke Energy Holding Corp. and changed its name to Duke Energy Corporation in April 2006. Duke Energy Corporation was founded in 1904 and is headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina.
